application.surface: The findings of the SaasReport reports

architecture.flow: The engine computes the figures for this month and the month before, and each published rule that matches becomes a finding with its evidence.

items.action: Churned MRR of USD 897.00 was larger than new MRR in the same period.
items.outcome: Compare what was added with what was lost this period and decide whether acquisition or retention needs attention first.

items.action: Refunds issued as fraudulent this period: 1.
items.outcome: Review the payments refunded as fraudulent and check whether your fraud rules, for example in Stripe Radar, need tightening.
Open the disputes that still need a response in the Stripe Dashboard and submit evidence before each deadline.

items.action: Net revenue retention was 81.08%: existing customers brought in less revenue than they did at the start of the period.
items.outcome: Look at the customers behind churned and contraction revenue and note the likely cause of each (price, fit, a failed payment, or a change on their side).

items.action: The payment failure rate rose to 11.67% from 6.00%.
items.outcome: Check how failed subscription payments are retried and how customers are told about them, in your Stripe Billing settings.

items.action: The refund rate rose to 6.83% from 3.90%.
items.outcome: Read a sample of this period's refunds, group them by reason, and act on the largest group first.

items.action: Refunds for duplicate charges this period: 1.
items.outcome: Check how checkout or your integration could create the same charge twice, for example double submits or retries without an idempotency key.

items.action: Net platform fees fell 0.76% to USD 263.97, from USD 266.00.
items.outcome: Check whether fee settings, pricing tiers or the mix of sellers and categories changed during the period, and compare the fee earned per payment against the prior period.

items.action: The take rate fell to 9.00%, from 10.00%.
items.outcome: Check whether fee settings, pricing tiers or the mix of sellers and categories changed during the period, and compare the fee earned per payment against the prior period.

items.action: Net new MRR was USD 100.00: more recurring revenue arrived than left.
items.outcome: Note what drove the gain (new, expansion or fewer losses) so it can be repeated.

application.surface: The report pipeline of the SaasReport app

architecture.flow: Stripe data is stored per tenant, turned into figures and findings, worded, rendered to a PDF, stored, and sent as a signed link.

stages.outcome: Charges, refunds, disputes and subscriptions arrive through the Stripe app, and are stored under your tenant only.
A deterministic engine turns the data into integers under published definitions.
Published rules read the figures and state what changed, with the evidence.
The AI sees aggregates only. A number guard rejects any number the engine did not compute.
The report is saved under your tenant's own prefix.
The reader gets a link that expires. The email carries no figures.
